messages:
Jamie: Heads-up — in canary today we saw p99 jump from ~280ms to ~1.2s under sustained ~600 rps. Correlates with KV cache miss spikes (cache occupancy ~98%). More tail when microbatch size >= 8.
Ashok: I saw this on the loadrunner a few hours ago. KV evictions spike, causing more cold KV fetches and the runtime to switch to a slower attention kernel. Can you paste profs?
Jamie: Quick profile snippet from the spike window:
```
p95: 310ms
p99: 1.2s
KV miss rate: 23% -> 76% during window
avg microbatch size: 9
kernel: attention_opt_v2 -> fallback generic_attention
worker: w-12 (host3)
```
Maria: That fallback path is heavy — it loses several fused ops and serializes a few kernels. Usually happens when sequence length distribution suddenly widens (many short + occasional long).
Theo: Suspect our kernel-selector cache. We cache chosen kernels per-worker and don't re-evaluate quickly on workload change (microbatch hysteresis). If we ramp batch size up, selector sticks to previous kernel and ends up picking conservative fallback.
Priya: Short-term mitigation: force the canary to use seq-optimized kernels and drop microbatch to 4. See if tail disappears.
Ashok: Also propose changing eviction tuning: when occupancy > 95% switch to LFU-soft + prefetch eligible keys instead of immediate full eviction. That should reduce churn on hot prefixes.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary update rolled: canary/kv-thrash -> microbatch=4, kernel_override=seq-opt, eviction_policy=lfu-soft.
Maria: Results from 15m post-deploy: p99 -> 380ms, p95 -> 220ms, KV miss rate down to 12%. CPU on worker4 increased ~8% but within headroom.
Jamie: Good improvement. There's still a 30-120ms tail on ~1% of requests. Those align with background disk compaction on host3 during test window. Need to isolate host noise.
Ashok: Action items: (1) run microbatch sweep [2,4,6,8] with kernel forced, (2) instrument and flame the KV fetch path (including disk vs mem), (3) add metric kernel-changes-per-minute per-worker and eviction-churn-rate.
Theo: I'll add a synthetic harness that reproduces freq of short requests with rare long requests to exercise selector. Also plan: stop caching kernel selection when cache_pressure > 90% (force selector re-eval).
Priya: Rough timeline? Can we stabilize before next public deploy?
Jamie: Aim to finish sweep + metrics by EOD tomorrow. If numbers hold we can roll to prod next week. Posting logs and graphs when sweep finishes. @here :thumbsup:
SRE-Bot: FYI scheduled perf collection rule enabled on canary for 24h.
Ashok: Debug trace command I'm using:
```
./perf_collect --pid $WORKER_PID --events kv_fetch,attention_kernel_change,kv_eviction --out /tmp/trace.json
```
Maria: Nice. If we can keep p99 < 400ms at target throughput with microbatch<=4 and kernel tweaks, we can relax the eviction aggressiveness.
Jamie: Ok will update thread with sweep CSV and flamegraphs. Thanks all :party_parrot:
